::: {.hero}
# Day 3: Deep Learning for Earth Observation

### U-Net Segmentation, SAR Flood Mapping and Object Detection

Leveraging neural networks for advanced EO image analysis
:::

## Day 3 Overview

Day 3 explores **advanced deep learning techniques** for Earth Observation, focusing on semantic segmentation and object detection. You'll learn the U-Net architecture for pixel-wise tasks like flood mapping, train one on real labelled Sentinel-1 flood data, and learn modern object detection methods (YOLO, Faster R-CNN) for locating and counting objects in satellite imagery. Philippine case studies — Central Luzon typhoon flooding and Metro Manila urban monitoring — frame how the methods are applied.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Sessions and materials

- **Session 1:** Semantic Segmentation with U-Net — lecture + slides
- **Session 2:** Flood Mapping Lab (U-Net + Sentinel-1 SAR) — runnable PyTorch notebook
- **Session 3:** Object Detection Techniques — lecture + slides
- **Session 4:** Object Detection Lab (Transfer Learning) — guided walkthrough with verified code snippets; links to runnable reference notebooks (no dedicated notebook in this edition)
:::

## Learning Objectives

By the end of Day 3, you will be able to:

::: {.learning-objectives}
- **Understand** U-Net encoder-decoder architecture and skip connections for semantic segmentation
- **Explain** the differences between semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and object detection
- **Implement** U-Net models from scratch in PyTorch (with TensorFlow/Keras reference code) for pixel-wise classification
- **Process** Sentinel-1 SAR imagery for flood detection and disaster response applications
- **Train** semantic segmentation models with dice loss and IoU metrics
- **Apply** U-Net to real flood events and plan its transfer to Philippine cases such as Central Luzon
- **Comprehend** object detection architectures (YOLO, Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet)
- **Calculate** object detection metrics including mAP, IoU, precision, and recall
- **Implement** transfer learning with pre-trained backbone networks (ResNet, MobileNet)
- **Fine-tune** pre-trained object detection models for new EO object classes (e.g. buildings)
- **Design** data augmentation strategies appropriate for EO tasks
- **Handle** imbalanced datasets using weighted loss functions and sampling strategies
- **Evaluate** segmentation quality using confusion matrices, IoU, and F1-scores
- **Visualize** model predictions and error patterns
- **Deploy** operational workflows for disaster mapping and urban monitoring
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Data used on Day 3

- **Session 2** trains on a subset of the public **Cloud to Street – Microsoft Flood Dataset (C2S-MS Floods)**:
  hand-labelled Sentinel-1 chips from 18 flood events worldwide (CC BY 4.0), downloaded directly from the open AWS
  bucket by the notebook. It contains no Philippine events; the Central Luzon case study shows how to transfer the model.
- **Session 4** uses public aerial detection datasets (e.g. Ultralytics `dota8`) for practice; no annotated
  Metro Manila dataset ships with the course.
- For your own Philippine data, Sentinel-1/-2 are available from the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem, Google Earth
  Engine and the CopPhil Mirror Site hosted by PhilSA.
:::
